Research supports goal drift as a studied failure mode in extended agent tasks; severity depends on task, model and scaffold.

The cited study does not establish inevitable onset after 100,000 tokens; it reports nearly perfect adherence by its best-performing scaffolded model beyond 100,000 tokens in its hardest setting while still finding some drift across evaluated models.
The 2026 preprint reports a steering agent improving performance/efficiency in information-seeking tasks. This is emerging research, not a universal or production-validated guarantee.
The checked sources do not establish that a binding/commitment split drives goal drift nearly to zero. No quantitative promise should be repeated without a named evaluation and baseline.

ERC-8004 is an agent discovery/trust-related standard proposal; it does not replace application-local authentication, authorization, tenant isolation or policy enforcement.

A trusted execution environment can provide bounded isolation/attestation properties; it does not by itself make the whole agent, its inputs, tools, policies or external effects trustworthy.
